Subject: Hosted pilot readiness — quickstart checklist, rate caps & fallback plan

Hi Ellie —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: integrate hosted API for customer-facing summarization + search augmentation.
- Traffic profile: initial pilot ~5k requests/day, peak 60 RPS for short bursts, median concurrency ~10.
- Data sensitivity: some records contain PII; Ledgerly is evaluating PHI implications and will confirm scope.

Proposed hosted quickstart (what we can enable within 2 business days)
1) Provision ephemeral staging endpoints (canary and main) mapped to your dev org.
2) Apply a pilot rate bucket: baseline 20 RPS, burst up to 100 RPS with autoscaling buffer.
3) Enable prefix KV caching for repeat prompts (saves tokens for chat flows).
4) Provide SOC2 summary & onboarding checklist for procurement.

Attachments & links
- Redwood quickstart checklist (attached): actionable items, API keys, example curl/SDK calls.
- Network onboarding guide (attached): IP ranges, egress expectations, TLS/KMS notes.
- Hosted docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstart/hosted

Open questions for you
- Can you confirm whether the pilot will include any PHI (yes/no)?
- Expected steady-state RPS after pilot (ballpark)?
- Do you need a VPC peering option for staging, or is public-hosted acceptable for now?

Next steps
- If okay, I’ll spin up the staging endpoints and share keys.
- Schedule a 30-min ops call with Aditya (solutions) and Naomi (billing) to finalize ratecaps and procurement checklist.

Proposed times: Thu Sep 24, 9:00–11:00 PT or Fri Sep 25, 13:00–15:00 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Ledgerly in a short hosted pilot.

—
Tessa Morgan

Thanks, Tessa — really helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) PHI: At this stage the dataset is mixed. We have a small subset that would be considered PHI if included — procurement needs confirmation from compliance, but we want to assume "sensitive" until told otherwise.
2) RPS: Pilot steady-state likely ~5–10 RPS, but as noted we have spikes (checkout flows) that could hit 40–80 RPS for ~30–120s at a time.
3) Caching: How persistent is the KV/prefix cache across requests? If a user hits 5 different shards will that reduce cache effectiveness?
4) Dedicated threshold: if we exceed sustained 500k tokens/day or consistent 300 RPS sustained, is dedicated capacity the recommended path?

We would like a hosted pilot but need assurance on data handling and a path to move to private/Dedicated if required. Please loop in your solutions engineer for the technicals and procurement for SOC2.

Can do Thu Sep 24 at 10:00 PT for the ops call.

Ellie Park

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Park <ellie@ledgerly.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted pilot readiness — quickstart checklist, rate caps & fallback plan

Hi Ellie — looping in with answers to the technical questions and a few config suggestions. Short answers first, then details.

Short answers
- KV/prefix cache: session-affine and per-backend. For hosted endpoints we maintain an in-memory KV cache on the serving cluster; it is session-scoped for chat flows and TTL-based (default 30 minutes). Cross-shard consistency: cache is not globally synchronized across isolated GPU shards — repeated prefixes routed to the same shard will hit cache; we can configure sticky-routing for pilot endpoints to improve cache hit rate.
- Dedicated threshold: your numbers (500k tokens/day or sustained 300 RPS) are reasonable heuristics where Dedicated makes sense for predictable unit economics and SLAs. We’ll provide modeling to confirm.
- PHI: Hosted (public) endpoints are encrypted in transit and at rest. For regulated PHI workloads we recommend Private (VPC) or On-prem. That said, many customers run sensitive-but-not-regulated workloads on Hosted with contractual controls; we will share the SOC2 summary and a data processing addendum for procurement to evaluate.

Network & region notes
- We can pin pilot endpoints to us-west1 or us-east1. If you need lower latency for your users in the east, we recommend us-east1. IP ranges and egress are in the attached network-onboarding-guide.pdf.

Ratecaps & fallback configuration (proposed pilot values)
- Baseline bucket: 20 RPS (steady).
- Burst policy: allow short bursts up to 120 RPS for 2 minutes; autoscaling buffer to 200 RPS for exceptional spikes.
- Throttling behavior: 429s with Retry-After; automated fallback to a smaller, cheaper model (if configured) when capacity constrained.
- Canary endpoints: we’ll create /v1/hosted/canary and /v1/hosted/staging so you can test rollout and warm caches.

Attachments: network-onboarding-guide.pdf and SOC2_summary.pdf included. I’ll also drop a short runbook into the drive link Tessa shared.

If Thu 10:00 PT works, I’ll send a calendar invite with a quick agenda: 1) confirm PHI scope and procurement docs, 2) finalize pilot ratecaps and sticky-routing, 3) handoff keys+canary endpoints.

—
Aditya Rao
